clue.text: Old soldier puts tree, sawn up, in the vehicle

indicators.note: in places the rearranged wood inside the word for the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: timber that is sawn up is cut into pieces, so the letters of the word tree are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old soldier loads a felled, sawn-up tree into his van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldier' could suggest VET, but the full phrase is the definition; 'sawn up' and 'in' are the operations, and 'puts' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long service, especially a former member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Against the Spanish surgeon having the material

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against
el is the Spanish word for the
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a Spanish surgeon having some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvet is a soft fabric with a dense pile.

clue.text: Number might try to hit out first

indicators.note: first places the shuffled hit at the front of the answer
out says the letters of the word hit are knocked out of their order
might suggests the letters of try might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A batsman thinks he might try to hit out right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns HIT into THI and 'might' turns TRY into RTY; 'first' puts THI ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty is a whole number, three tens.

clue.text: How a military unit was systematically organised?

definitions.text: How a military unit was systematically organised?

parts.words: How a military unit was systematically organised?
parts.note: a body of soldiers formed into a regiment would be organised this way, and the word also means strictly ordered in general

explanation.definitionFit: Something forced into a rigid, orderly system is said to be organised like an army unit.

clue.text: Titled gentleman heard in the darkness

indicators.note: heard says the word for the titled gentleman is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a knight is a man given the title Sir

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman can be heard moving about in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between dusk and dawn are the night.

clue.text: Agreeable pupil leaving countryman

indicators.note: leaving says the pupil goes out of the word for agreeable

parts.note: pleasant means agreeable
L, for learner, stands for a pupil, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A pleasant pupil leaves school to work the land.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate, so L stands for a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a farm worker or rustic, a man of the country.

clue.text: Literary work found on the stove?

definitions.meaning: a book written quickly for money, a hack novel
taken literally, a pot that boils sits on a cooker

explanation.definitionFit: A hack book churned out to keep the pot boiling is named for a cooking vessel heating on a hob.

clue.text: Wine from Italia still? No, it's sparkling

indicators.note: from says the wine is taken out of the following words, spanning their join

explanation.surface: Is the Italian wine still or sparkling? It's sparkling.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'ItaliA STIll'; the remark about sparkling fits, since the Piedmont wine is usually sparkling.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a white wine from Piedmont, often sparkling as Asti Spumante.

clue.text: Large tunny swimming round a coral bed endlessly

indicators.note: swimming round pictures the letters moving about, so they are rearranged
endlessly says the word bed loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A big tuna swims around a coral reef bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BED to BE; 'swimming round' then mixes A CORAL with BE.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned species of tuna, and tunny is an old name for tuna.

clue.text: Giving free medical attention?

definitions.meaning: standing someone a drink or meal at your own expense
a doctor caring for a patient

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both paying for another's pleasure and a doctor caring for the sick.

clue.text: Deceptively recumbent

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both telling falsehoods and stretched out horizontally.

clue.text: Obtain an item of furniture that is accessible

parts.note: to get is to obtain
an gives A, the indefinite article
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Buy a table that you can easily reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily reached or obtained is informally called get-at-able.

clue.text: Reckoning I am in the eastern depot

indicators.note: in puts the short form for I am inside the depot

parts.note: a station is a depot for trains or buses
I'm is the contracted form of I am, giving I and M

explanation.surface: Someone calculates their whereabouts in an eastern depot.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoning means a judgement or calculation, an assessment.

clue.text: The last one sees of the rabbit

definitions.text: The last one sees of the rabbit

parts.words: The last one sees of the rabbit
parts.note: as a rabbit bolts away, the final glimpse is its short white tail

explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short tail of a rabbit, hare or deer, seen as it runs off.

clue.text: Made a ruling-on paper only?

parts.note: ruling here is drawing a line with a ruler, not a judge's decision, so a line was drawn beneath words on a page

explanation.definitionFit: Emphasising text by drawing a line beneath it is making a ruled line on paper.

clue.text: Performing like marathon athletes ultimately

definitions.meaning: taking part in a race over a great distance

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means eventually, and literally describes competitors in a long-distance race.

clue.text: Go to bed at the farm?

definitions.meaning: literally, striking dried grass in a barn

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for retiring to sleep literally pictures striking dried grass on a farm.

clue.text: Unattractive cleaning woman?

parts.note: a woman who scrubs floors, and also British slang for a coarse, unattractive woman

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a coarse woman also describes someone who scrubs.

clue.text: Delirious if centre is removed

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters are shifted from their places and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone becomes frantic when the centre is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' and 'removed' look like a deletion, but the whole phrase IF CENTRE is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frenzied, wildly excited.

clue.text: Woodworker with a sting in his tail

definitions.text: Woodworker with a sting in his tail

parts.words: Woodworker with a sting in his tail
parts.note: a joiner with a sting suggests an insect that bores into timber

explanation.definitionFit: This solitary insect tunnels into wood to nest and can sting.

clue.text: Man accepting alternative spirit

indicators.note: accepting means the word for man takes in the other piece

parts.note: male means a man
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A man embraces an alternative spirituality.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is the confidence and spirit of a person or group.

clue.text: Obliquely across the French book

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Obliquely across the French book' gives only LA (the French) and NT (book) for the end of ASLANT; nothing in 'across' gives AS, so the clue looks misread (likely 'as').

clue.text: Bony part of incomplete lunar construction

indicators.note: construction suggests the letters are built into a new arrangement
incomplete says the word lunar loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A bone forms part of an unfinished lunar building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts LUNAR to LUNA, and 'construction' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Gallant chorus Val and I produced

indicators.note: produced suggests a staged show, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A chorus line featuring Val and the speaker puts on a gallant show.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalrous means courteous and brave, like a knight.

clue.text: See nothing on the recorder

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing shows up on the recorder.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recording machine, short for video recorder.

clue.text: Go on board

definitions.meaning: a turn in chess or draughts

explanation.definitionFit: A player's turn and a piece's shift on a chessboard are both this word.

clue.text: Engaged the debtor with difficulty

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters are rearranged awkwardly

explanation.surface: Someone found it hard to hire the debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrothed means promised in marriage, engaged to be wed.

clue.text: Could be any South African lake

indicators.note: could be says the letters of any might be put in another order

parts.note: SA is short for South Africa

explanation.surface: A lake that could be anywhere in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Nyasa, now Lake Malawi, is a great lake of East Africa.

clue.text: One hundred less cups and saucers found in the garden

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase for a garden feature, read as a noun

indicators.note: less means the hundred is subtracted from the tableware

parts.note: crockery is cups, saucers and plates
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Broken cups and saucers turn up buried in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is a garden bed built of stones and alpine plants.

clue.text: Singular item intended, say, to be left over

definitions.note: the definition describes a remnant, read as a noun for a leftover piece

parts.note: odd means singular, peculiar

indicators.note: say signals that the word for intended is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A peculiar item was meant to remain unused.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a remnant or scrap remaining after the rest is used.
